about: The ruler of `npm run check:visual`: which reference states are measured, how, and how far from them still passes. Changing this file changes the measurement, which is why docs/loop/done.toml protects it.
browser: Playwright's Chromium, headless, device scale factor 1
clockNote: Fixed so the live clocks and ages cannot move between runs. The recording is replayed as of this instant, so the approval reads esperando · 1:35 and the turn 1m42s, as in the references.

reference.dirNote: Relative to the repository root, where the images are committed. Override with --refs <dir> or DCODE_DESIGN_SCREENSHOTS.
reference.cropNote: The references are 1602×962: the mock's window element with its 1px border. The window's content is the 1600×960 inside it, which is what the renderer draws. The four corners outside the window's 12px radius differ by construction (about a hundred pixels).

windowControls: drawn: in fixture mode (a plain browser, no native controls) the renderer draws the same three 12px placeholders the mock draws, so the title-bar strip is compared, not masked.
pixelmatchNote: threshold is pixelmatch's per-pixel colour distance (0–1); anti-aliased pixels are not counted, so glyph edges do not register as differences.
maxMismatchNote: Chosen from the first honest run after the visible differences were fixed, and anchored to the design, not to the window.

Floor: the handoff's own HTML mock, rendered by this same Chromium with the pointer parked and the clock at 1:35, scores 1.15% (02) and 1.19% (03) under this ruler. The references were rasterised elsewhere: the glyphs are identical, but that renderer does not round Geist's ascent and descent the way Chrome on macOS does, so baselines land a pixel apart row by row. No CSS removes that; setting line-height to Geist's exact 1.3 moved the score by at most 0.12 points and pulled the window 0.9 points away from the mock as this engine draws it.

The window scores 1.17% (02) and 1.19% (03), identical pixel counts on repeated runs. Against the mock rendered by this Chromium it is 0.20% and 0.12% apart, and every remaining difference is a gap recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md or a deliberate choice there (the bottom bar says gravação, not daemon; no ↵ on the approval).

1.25% is the smallest round limit the design's own mock passes on both states, leaving about 900 pixels for rasterisation differences between machines. A missing or moved element costs more than that; a shift of a pixel or two does not register — moving the whole flow by 2px changed the score by 0.10 points, the wrong way. For work finer than that, compare with the mock rendered here.
When the references change (a new Claude Design version), measure the new mock's floor the same way and revise this limit deliberately: it is part of the ruler, and docs/loop/done.toml protects it.
